Reporter: Your school bus stops two streets from school. Would you like it to stop at the gate?
Jin: No. My friend meets me at the bus stop. We walk the last part together.

Reporter: But the gate would be nearer.
Jin: Yes. On the bus, I sit beside my little brother. At school, my friend is in another class. Those two streets are our time.

Reporter: Even on a cold day?
Jin: I bring my coat. She brings hers.
question: What kind of text is this?
correct: An interview with a student about a school journey.
wrong1: A public notice announcing a new school bus stop.
wrong2: A student's diary about walking home from school.
wrong3: A bus company advert for faster school journeys.
explanation: A reporter asks Jin questions, and Jin answers about the journey to school.
source: Original. Imagined interview on road safety; people, places, organisations, events and numerical results are fictional.
question2: What is the main idea of the text?
correct2: Jin values time with a friend more than a shorter journey.
wrong1_2: Jin wants a nearer bus stop to avoid walking in the cold.
wrong2_2: Jin walks because the bus cannot reach the school gate.
wrong3_2: Jin wants a different bus so the friends can sit together.
explanation2: Walking takes longer, but it gives Jin time with a friend. Jin does not want the stop at the gate.

title: The Slow Video
passage:
I wanted to see how our bean plant grew, so I watched it for an hour. Nothing seemed to happen. My sister said I needed a longer video, not more time beside the window.

We took one photo each morning for two weeks. Then we put the photos together on the computer and played them quickly. The little plant opened and moved towards the light in seconds.

I watched that short video five times. Two weeks fitted between my breakfast and the bus. You can watch my video below.
question: What kind of text is this?
correct: A blog post about trying a plant project.
wrong1: A science report giving results from many farms.
wrong2: A camera advert showing how to make videos.
wrong3: A diary entry about a plant lesson at school.
explanation: The writer shares a personal project with online readers rather than writing a formal study.
source: Original. Imagined blog post on science; people, places, organisations, events and numerical results are fictional.
question2: What is the main idea of the text?
correct2: Playing daily photos quickly made the plant's slow growth easy to see.
wrong1_2: Keeping a camera near the plant made the plant grow much faster.
wrong2_2: Watching the plant for an hour showed more than two weeks of photos.
wrong3_2: The sister made a longer video by filming the plant for one morning.
explanation2: An hour of watching showed little. Playing two weeks of photos quickly made the plant's changes easy to see.
